intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon Dynasty palace and rent a traditional Hanbok to wear while wandering the palace grounds. Wearing Hanbok grants free entry and makes for stunning cultural photos. Nearby Bukchon Hanok Village offers a glimpse into traditional Korean architecture and daily life.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). A must-do for any local food enthusiast wanting an authentic culinary experience.

experiences.name: K-Pop Dance Class & Idol District Exploration
experiences.description: Take a beginner K-Pop dance class at one of Hongdae's many entertainment studios, learning choreography from popular idol groups. Afterward, explore the Hongdae street art scene, live busking performances, and indie K-culture shops. This neighborhood is the heartbeat of Korea's youth and pop culture scene.

experiences.name: Incheon Songdo & Eurwangni Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a short trip from Seoul to Incheon's Eurwangni Beach, one of the closest accessible beachfront areas to Seoul. Enjoy the sandy shores, fresh seafood restaurants along the coast, and the futuristic Songdo International Business District. This is the best option for a beachfront experience within easy reach of Seoul.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Arts & Traditional Tea Ceremony
experiences.description: Stroll through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional Korean crafts, antique shops, and contemporary galleries. Participate in a guided traditional Korean tea ceremony at a historic teahouse, learning about the philosophy and rituals behind Korean tea culture. End the evening exploring the Ssamziegil courtyard complex.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Focus on transit from Incheon Airport to hotel. Take the AREX Airport Express train to Seoul Station (₩9,500), then transfer via subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station. Check in to Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Once settled, take a short walk to explore the immediate Gyeongbokgung neighbourhood. Stroll along Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and enjoy the atmosphere of Bukchon Hanok Village's nearby alleys — no entry fee, perfect for a gentle first afternoon. Pop into a convenience store (CU or GS25) for any immediate snack needs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong (10-min walk) for a relaxed first evening. Explore the Ssamziegil courtyard, browse indie shops, and soak in the K-culture street vibe. Grab dinner at one of the many affordable pojangmacha (street food tents) or a local Korean restaurant along Insadong-gil.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a kimbap roll (₩1,500) from a convenience store near the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Seoul Station — try a bowl of instant ramyeon or a set meal at a station food court (₩6,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong area: Jjigae (stew) set meal at a local restaurant such as Doore Restaurant — sundubu-jjigae or doenjang-jjigae with rice and banchan (₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Get a T-money card at the airport or any convenience store (₩2,500 + top-up) for seamless subway and bus travel throughout the trip. December in Seoul is cold (around -2°C to 5°C), so layer up immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace right at opening time (9:00 AM). Admission is ₩3,000. If you rent a hanbok from one of the nearby rental shops (₩15,000–20,000 for 2 hours), entry to the palace is FREE. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM at Gwanghwamun Gate — spectacular and free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free entry). After, head to Cheongwadae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence opened to the public — for a free guided tour (book online in advance at cheongwadae.go.kr). Walk along the scenic Bugaksan mountain trail behind it if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Gwanghwamun Square in the evening when it is lit up beautifully in winter. Walk to nearby Sejong-daero for street food vendors. Head back to Insadong or try Euljiro area for a trendy local bar or café experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel: triangle kimbap + hot coffee (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) near Gyeongbokgung — a Seoul institution. One bowl costs ₩17,000 but is hearty and worth it as a splurge lunch
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area street food: hotteok (sweet pancake ₩1,500), odeng (fish cake skewer ₩1,000), and tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes ₩3,000) from street stalls

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays, but Day 2 is Wednesday so it is open. Arrive early to avoid crowds. The hanbok rental is a wonderful K-culture experience and saves the entrance fee. Dress very warmly — palace grounds are exposed and windy in December.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Bukchon Hanok Village — a free, self-guided walk through preserved traditional Korean hanok houses. Follow the official Bukchon 8 scenic spots map (available free at the nearby tourist information center). Best in the morning before tour groups arrive. Enjoy the view of tiled rooftops against the backdrop of Namsan Tower.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon). Admission: ₩3,000 for palace, ₩5,000 for Secret Garden guided tour. The Secret Garden is one of Seoul's most beautiful and tranquil spaces — especially atmospheric in winter with frost on the trees. Book the English guided tour slot online.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) via subway (Line 5, Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station). The DDP's futuristic architecture is stunning at night and free to walk around. Check out the Dongdaemun Night Market for street food and budget shopping. Great for K-culture fashion browsing.

meals.breakfast: Nearby café in Bukchon: Korean-style breakfast of kongnamul-gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) at a local diner (₩6,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Anguk-dong area: Noryangjin-style bibimbap at a local restaurant near Changdeokgung (₩8,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun Night Market street food feast: tteokbokki, sundae (Korean blood sausage), twigim (fried snacks) — full meal for under ₩8,000

day_by_day.notes: Bukchon Hanok Village residents still live there — please be quiet and respectful, especially in the early morning. The Secret Garden guided tour times are limited; book ahead. Dongdaemun area is buzzing until late — great for night owls.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station. Explore Myeongdong Cathedral (free entry, beautiful Gothic architecture) and the surrounding streets. Visit the underground Myeongdong Shopping Street for affordable K-beauty products — many brands offer free samples. Budget K-beauty brands like Innisfree, The Face Shop, and Etude House have flagship stores here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a cable car (₩9,500 round trip) up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) on Namsan Mountain. The observation deck costs ₩21,000 but the outdoor deck and the walk through Namsan Park are free. Hang a love lock on the famous lock fence. Alternatively, hike up the Namsan trail for free panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the famous evening street food market that comes alive after dark. Dozens of vendors line the streets with lobster, corn dogs, egg bread, and more. Then explore nearby Namdaemun Market — one of Korea's oldest traditional markets — for late evening shopping and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area: find a local bakery like Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for a pastry and coffee (₩4,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong: Kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) at Myeongdong Kyoja — a Seoul legend. A bowl costs ₩12,000 and is incredibly filling
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food: egg bread (gyeran-ppang ₩2,000), Korean corn dog (₩3,000–4,000), hotteok (₩1,500) — eat your way down the street for under ₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is very touristy but the street food and K-beauty shopping are genuinely excellent value. Friday evenings are lively. Namsan cable car can have queues — consider hiking up instead (30–40 min walk) for free and great exercise.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the heartbeat of Seoul's youth K-culture scene. Arrive in the morning to explore the indie art shops, street murals, and quirky cafés. Visit the Trick Eye Museum (₩15,000) or the nearby Hongdae Free Market (weekends only, free entry) where local artists sell handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Edae (Ewha Womans University) area. The Ewha campus is architecturally stunning and free to explore — the underground ECC building is a must-see. Browse the affordable fashion and food streets around Sinchon. Take the subway to Mangwon Market (Line 6) for a local, non-touristy traditional market experience.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the Saturday night K-indie music scene. Street buskers perform nightly near Hongdae Exit 9 — completely free and incredibly entertaining. Explore the club and bar district if interested (many free entry before 10 PM). Norebang (karaoke) rooms are a quintessential K-culture experience — rent a private room for ₩15,000–20,000 per hour split among friends.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae: Brunch at a trendy but affordable café — avocado toast or Korean egg sandwich (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market: fresh bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes ₩3,000), tteokbokki, and gimbap — a full market lunch for ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae: Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a local BBQ restaurant — order 2 portions with soju for a satisfying dinner (₩15,000–18,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in Hongdae are electric — embrace the energy. The area is very safe and walkable. Norebang is a must-do K-culture activity; look for places advertising 낮 (day) rates for cheaper daytime slots. Mangwon Market is beloved by locals and far less crowded than Gwangjang.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's most famous and oldest traditional markets, and a food lover's paradise. Arrive early (around 9 AM) when it is less crowded. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini gimbap), and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare) — all at incredibly low prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream running through the heart of Seoul. The walk from Gwangjang to City Hall area is about 3 km and completely free. In December it is decorated with winter light installations. Visit the nearby Seoul Museum of History (free entry) to learn about the city's transformation.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jongno 3-ga area, known for its unique pojangmacha culture and the famous Nakwon Arcade (Asia's largest musical instrument market — fascinating to browse even without buying). Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a hip neighbourhood of converted hanok houses turned into indie cafés, bars, and boutiques. Perfect for a Sunday evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market: mayak kimbap (₩3,000 for a plate) and a bowl of kongnamul-gukbap (₩5,000) — a legendary Seoul breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market continued: bindaetteok (₩4,000 each) and a bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) from a nearby market restaurant (₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Ikseon-dong: trendy but affordable Korean fusion at one of the hanok cafés — try a set meal of Korean-style pasta or traditional tteok desserts with sikhye (sweet rice drink) for ₩10,000–12,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is a UNESCO-recognized cultural heritage food destination — do not skip it. Sundays are busy but the atmosphere is wonderful. Ikseon-dong is one of Seoul's most Instagrammable neighbourhoods and very popular with young Koreans — great for K-culture immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — one of Korea's most historically significant and unique experiences. Book a budget DMZ tour through a local agency (around ₩40,000–55,000 including transport and guide). Tours depart from central Seoul around 8:00–9:00 AM. Visit the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel and the Dora Observatory overlooking North Korea.
day_by_day.afternoon: The DMZ tour typically includes Imjingak Park (free to explore independently), the Freedom Bridge, and Dorasan Station — the southernmost train station built in hope of future reunification. Return to Seoul by late afternoon (tours usually return by 5–6 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Gyeongbokgung area and enjoy a quiet evening. Visit the Tongin Market nearby for a fun and unique budget dinner experience — buy old-fashioned Korean coins (₩5,000 for 10 coins) and use them to buy small dishes from different vendors in the market's dosirak (lunchbox) café.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab convenience store kimbap and canned coffee before the tour bus (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Included in most DMZ tours or available at Imjingak Park food stalls — Korean army stew (budae-jjigae) is popular in this region (₩10,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Tongin Market dosirak experience: fill your lunchbox with assorted banchan dishes using the coin system — a full and fun dinner for ₩5,000–8,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the DMZ tour at least 2–3 days in advance as spots fill up. Bring your passport — it is required for entry. Photography rules are strict; follow the guide's instructions. This is the most expensive day of the trip but offers unparalleled historical and cultural insight. Tongin Market coin lunchbox experience is a beloved Seoul tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Seodaemun Prison History Hall (₩3,000 admission) — a former Japanese colonial-era prison that is now a powerful museum documenting Korea's independence movement. Deeply moving and essential for understanding modern Korean history and culture. Located near Dongnimmun (Independence Gate), which is free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sinchon/Yonsei University area and walk through the beautiful Yonsei campus. Then take the subway to Hapjeong and walk along the Hongdae-Hapjeong café strip. Visit the Gyeongui Line Forest Park (Gyeongui-seon Supra) — a linear park built on a former railway line, similar to New York's High Line. Free and lovely for a winter afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Mapo-gu's Mangwon or Hapjeong area for dinner — these neighbourhoods have excellent local restaurants frequented by young Koreans. Explore the independent bookshops, vinyl record stores, and small galleries that populate this creative district. Very authentic K-culture neighbourhood feel.

meals.breakfast: Near Seodaemun: local Korean breakfast restaurant serving haejang-guk (hangover soup / hearty morning stew) — ₩8,000–9,000
meals.lunch: Sinchon area: dosirak (Korean lunch box) restaurant where you choose your own toppings — filling and cheap at ₩7,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Hapjeong/Mangwon: dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a local restaurant — ₩12,000–14,000 per person, excellent value

day_by_day.notes: Seodaemun Prison is closed on Mondays — but today is Tuesday, so it is open. The experience is sobering but essential for understanding the Korean spirit of resilience that underpins so much of modern K-culture. The Gyeongui Line park is especially pretty with winter decorations.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon (Line 6) and visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (admission ₩10,000) — one of Korea's finest private art museums with a stunning building designed by three world-renowned architects. Alternatively, visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (free entry) — one of the world's largest museums with incredible Korean artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Itaewon and Haebangchon (HBC) neighbourhoods — multicultural, eclectic, and full of character. Walk up the hill to Haebangchon for great views and indie cafés. Visit the nearby War Memorial of Korea (free entry) — an enormous and impressive museum covering Korean military history from ancient times to the Korean War.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Han River (Hangang) Park at Yeouido or Banpo for the evening. In winter, the park is quieter but atmospheric. Grab convenience store snacks and sit by the river — a beloved Korean pastime called 'chimaek' (chicken and beer). Watch for the Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain show if operating in winter.

meals.breakfast: Itaewon area: a rare treat — international breakfast options abound. Try a small local café for eggs and toast (₩7,000–8,000) or stick to convenience store for budget
meals.lunch: Haebangchon: local Korean restaurant serving jeyuk-bokkeum (spicy stir-fried pork) with rice and banchan — ₩9,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Han River convenience store dinner (a quintessential Seoul experience): cup ramyeon, kimbap, fried chicken from GS25 or CU — full meal under ₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is massive — allow at least 3 hours and focus on the highlights (prehistoric, Goryeo, and Joseon galleries). The Han River convenience store experience is genuinely one of the most beloved local activities in Seoul — embrace it fully. Check if the Banpo fountain is operating in December before making the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, located just minutes from the hotel. Entry is free. In late December, the temple is decorated with thousands of colourful lanterns for the upcoming New Year celebrations — absolutely magical. Attend a morning ceremony if you wake early (around 4 AM or 10 AM services).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts and the surrounding Gwanghwamun area. Visit the Sejong Story underground exhibition (free) about King Sejong and the creation of Hangul. Walk to Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae (near Gyeongbokgung) — a free exhibition space about Korean culture and the presidency.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is celebrated enthusiastically — especially in Myeongdong and Hongdae. Head to Myeongdong for the festive atmosphere, carol performances, and Christmas market stalls. The streets are beautifully decorated. Join young Koreans celebrating the holiday — it is one of the most festive and exciting nights of the year in the city.

meals.breakfast: Jogyesa area: traditional Korean breakfast at a temple-adjacent restaurant — doenjang-jjigae set (₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun area: bunsik (Korean snack food) restaurant serving kimbap, ramyeon, and tteokbokki — a full set for ₩7,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special: treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner in Myeongdong — Korean BBQ samgyeopsal at a busy restaurant, sharing the festive atmosphere with other diners (₩15,000–18,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — it is primarily celebrated as a couples' holiday but the city-wide festivity is infectious. Myeongdong will be extremely crowded but wonderfully atmospheric. Book any restaurant reservations in advance if you plan to splurge on dinner. Jogyesa's lantern decorations are a highlight not to miss.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike up Inwangsan Mountain — accessible directly from the Gyeongbokgung neighbourhood (about 20-min walk to the trailhead). The hike to the summit takes about 1 hour and offers breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul in winter. Pass by the shamanist Guksadang shrine along the trail — a fascinating glimpse into Korea's pre-Buddhist spiritual traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (free entry) located within the Gyeongbokgung complex — a beautifully curated museum of royal artifacts. Then explore Gyeonghuigung Palace (free entry) — a lesser-visited but charming palace near the hotel, perfect for a quiet Christmas afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Bukchon and Samcheong-dong area for a peaceful Christmas evening. Samcheong-dong is lined with lovely independent cafés, galleries, and boutiques. Find a cosy café for hot sikhye or traditional Korean teas. The neighbourhood is quiet and romantic on Christmas evening — a perfect contrast to the previous night's energy.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike: convenience store banana milk, kimbap, and energy bar (₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Post-hike reward: Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) — warming, nourishing, and perfect for a cold December day (₩17,000)
meals.dinner: Samcheong-dong: cosy Korean restaurant serving jeon (Korean pancakes) and makgeolli (traditional rice wine) — a set of assorted jeon with a jug of makgeolli for ₩15,000–18,000

day_by_day.notes: Many shops and restaurants may have reduced hours on Christmas Day — plan ahead and have backup options. The Inwangsan hike is moderately challenging; wear good shoes and dress in warm layers. Makgeolli and jeon pairing in a traditional Korean restaurant is one of the most authentic and enjoyable K-culture dining experiences available.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lotte World Tower area in Jamsil (take subway Line 2). The tower is the world's 5th tallest building — the observation deck (Seoul Sky) costs ₩29,000 but the mall, outdoor Seokchon Lake, and surrounding park are all free. Walk around Seokchon Lake for beautiful views of the tower reflected in the water. Lotte World Theme Park is adjacent if budget allows (₩62,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to COEX Mall in Gangnam (subway Line 2, Samseong Station) — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the stunning COEX Library (Starfield Library) — a massive public library/reading space with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves that is completely free and one of Seoul's most photogenic spaces. Browse the SM Town Museum for K-pop culture (admission ₩12,000).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gangnam-daero and the Gangnam Station area — the setting made famous by PSY's 'Gangnam Style.' Window shop along the upscale streets, then find a budget-friendly restaurant in the back alleys. Head to nearby Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Street) for a beautiful evening walk among boutique shops and cafés.

meals.breakfast: Jamsil area: local bakery or convenience store near the hotel before departing (₩4,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court: wide variety of Korean options — try a bowl of naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbitang (short rib soup) — ₩9,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam back alleys: find a sundubu-jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant — a warming and filling dinner for ₩9,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: The Starfield Library at COEX is one of Seoul's most impressive free attractions — do not miss it. SM Town Museum is worthwhile for K-pop fans. Gangnam is Seoul's most expensive district but budget eating is still very possible in the side streets. This is a great day to pick up any last-minute souvenirs at COEX.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favourite neighbourhood near the hotel. Take a slow morning walk through Gyeongbokgung area, stop at Jogyesa Temple one last time, and browse Insadong for any remaining souvenir shopping. Insadong has excellent and affordable traditional Korean souvenirs: hanji paper products, celadon ceramics, traditional teas, and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Museum of Craft Art (Craft Museum) in Bukchon — free entry, showcasing traditional Korean crafts including celadon, lacquerware, and embroidery. A wonderful final cultural experience. Then head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Check out and store luggage at the hotel if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Seoul — choose a restaurant that represents your favourite meal of the trip. Alternatively, visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) like Dragon Hill Spa for a final authentic Korean experience (₩12,000–15,000 entry). Relax, use the various hot pools, and enjoy the communal Korean spa culture before heading to the airport or resting for an early departure.

meals.breakfast: Insadong area: final Korean breakfast — haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake) and doenjang-jjigae set at a local restaurant (₩9,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market revisit: one last round of mayak kimbap and bindaetteok — the perfect farewell Seoul meal (₩6,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Celebratory final dinner: galbi (Korean BBQ short ribs) at a mid-range local restaurant near the hotel — a worthy send-off splurge (₩20,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time to get to the airport — AREX train from Seoul Station to Incheon takes about 43 minutes (₩9,500 direct). If your flight departs early the next morning, consider staying near the airport or booking the AREX in advance. Use any remaining T-money card balance on transit or convenience store purchases — the card is reloadable and keeps its balance. Take home a bag of Korean instant ramyeon, roasted seaweed, and honey butter chips as the perfect edible souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Incheon International Airport to hotel via AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Hongik University Station, then transfer to Line 3 toward Gyeongbokgung Station (~60-70 min total). Check in to boutique stay in Jongno-gu and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll around the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Walk along the iconic palace walls on Sajik-ro, explore the charming Seochon Village (서촌) just west of the palace — a quiet hanok alley district perfect for getting your bearings and soaking in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong (도보 15분) for a relaxed first evening. Browse the traditional craft shops and galleries along the main street, then settle in for dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at Incheon Airport (Paris Baguette or convenience store onigiri)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Seoul Station or Gyeongbokgung area — try a 편의점 (convenience store) kimbap and ramen to experience Korean convenience culture
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — famous ginseng chicken soup restaurant, perfect warming comfort food for December. ~15,000–18,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (typically -5°C to 5°C). Pack thermal layers, a heavy coat, gloves, and a scarf. The AREX express train costs ~9,500 KRW. T-money card recommended — purchase at the airport for seamless subway travel.

day_by_day.morning: Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) opening visit — arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon, the scenic Gyeonghoeru Pavilion (frozen pond in winter is magical), and Hyangwonjeong garden. Consider renting a hanbok at the entrance for free palace admission and beautiful photos. (~3 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌 한옥마을) — wander the steep alleyways lined with traditional Korean wooden houses. Visit the Bukchon Traditional Culture Center. Then head to nearby Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) for the UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (비원) guided tour (book in advance, ~8,000 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's main street more thoroughly — visit Ssamziegil courtyard complex for indie shops and K-culture goods. Enjoy the festive December street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby 해장국 (haejangguk) hangover soup restaurant — a classic Korean morning meal. ~8,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — a short taxi ride away. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and tteokbokki from market stalls. ~10,000–15,000 KRW total
meals.dinner: Jirisan (지리산) or a local 삼겹살 (samgyeopsal) BBQ spot in Insadong/Jongno area — grill your own pork belly at the table. ~15,000–20,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — perfect that today is Wednesday. Hanbok rental shops open around 9:00 AM near the main gate. Secret Garden tours run at set times; book online or arrive early. Wear comfortable walking shoes — cobblestones in Bukchon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums, free admission. Explore Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty. Highlights include the Silla gold crowns and Buddhist sculpture gallery. (~2.5 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon and the newly revitalized Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood. Browse the eclectic mix of international boutiques and K-culture shops. Then visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (리움미술관) — world-class collection of Korean traditional and contemporary art (~18,000 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Itaewon for the evening — explore the vibrant nightlife-adjacent streets, visit a themed café, and enjoy the multicultural energy of this district.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel — try a local bakery like Tartine or a Korean-style café for toast and coffee. ~6,000–9,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Museum restaurant or the museum grounds food court — affordable Korean set meals (~12,000 KRW)
meals.dinner: Itaewon's Local Kitchen — try Maple Tree House (메이플트리하우스) for high-quality Korean BBQ with a modern twist, or opt for a cozy pojangmacha (street tent bar) experience with fried chicken and beer (치맥). ~20,000–25,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Korea is free but check for any special exhibitions with separate ticketing. Take subway Line 4 to Ichon Station for the museum. Leeum is a 10-minute walk from Hangangjin Station (Line 6).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원 화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage site. Take the subway (Line 1, ~50 min from Seoul Station). Walk the fortress walls for panoramic views, visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and explore the traditional market inside the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional Suwon Yanggaengi Market. Return to Seoul by 4:00–5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Seoul, visit Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a beautifully lit urban stream walkway in central Seoul. In December it's decorated with winter light festivals. Walk the stream and enjoy the illuminations.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel or a quick 김밥천국 (Kimbap Cheonguk) chain meal. ~5,000–7,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its beef short ribs. Try a local galbi restaurant near Hwaseong for an authentic regional specialty. ~20,000–25,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market or Jongno 3-ga area for evening street food and pojangmacha — try sundae (blood sausage), odeng (fish cake skewers), and hot barley tea. ~10,000–15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is easily accessible via subway — no need for a tour bus. The fortress walk takes about 2–3 hours for the full circuit. Dress warmly as the fortress walls are exposed and windy in December. Cheonggyecheon light festival typically runs through January.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP, 동대문디자인플라자) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Browse design exhibitions and the outdoor plaza. Then walk to nearby Dongdaemun Market — one of the world's largest wholesale and retail clothing markets. Great for K-fashion finds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Naksan Park (낙산공원) — a hilltop park along the ancient Seoul City Wall with sweeping views of the city. Walk a section of the Hanyangdoseong (Seoul City Wall) trail. The park is particularly atmospheric in winter with clear skies.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's university district and K-culture epicenter. Experience the vibrant street performances, indie music scene, and youth culture. Visit the Free Market area (weekends) and explore the neon-lit streets.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market morning visit — try 육회 (yukhoe, raw beef) or 빈대떡 for a traditional Korean breakfast experience. ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — try Dokkaebi Market food stalls or a nearby 순대국밥 (sundae soup) restaurant. ~9,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Hongdae restaurant district — try Yoogane Dak Galbi (유가네 닭갈비) for spicy stir-fried chicken, a Hongdae staple. ~12,000–16,000 KRW. Follow with a famous Hongdae dessert café visit.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Hongdae will be very lively — great for people-watching and street performance culture. DDP sometimes hosts special winter exhibitions. Wear comfortable shoes for the Naksan wall walk — some steep sections. Hongdae is on subway Line 2.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located right in Jongno. In December it may be decorated with beautiful lanterns. Attend a morning ceremony if open to visitors. Then explore the surrounding Insadong-gil street for Sunday morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seochon Village (서촌) in depth — visit the Yun Dong-ju Poet's Hill, Cheongun Literary Garden (청운문학도서관), and the quirky independent bookshops and art galleries. Great neighborhood for slow travel and cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Myeongdong (명동) evening visit — Seoul's most famous shopping district is especially festive in December with Christmas markets and street food stalls. Shop for Korean skincare, cosmetics, and fashion. Experience the legendary street food alley.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near the hotel — 된장찌개 (doenjang jjigae, fermented soybean paste stew) with rice and banchan. ~8,000–10,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Seochon area café lunch — try Hyoja-dong Jatguksu (잣국수, pine nut noodles) — a unique local specialty. ~12,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food dinner — graze on tteokbokki, hotteok (sweet pancakes), corn dogs, and tornado potatoes. Budget ~15,000 KRW for a full street food spread. End with a sit-down 냉면 (naengmyeon, cold noodles) or 설렁탕 (seolleongtang, ox bone soup) at a traditional restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free to enter and centrally located — a peaceful contrast to the busy city. Myeongdong is crowded on Sunday evenings but the festive December atmosphere is worth it. Great for K-beauty shopping — Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young all have flagship stores here.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) and Petite France — take a morning bus or organized shuttle from Myeongdong (~1.5 hrs). Nami Island is famous for its tree-lined paths and K-drama filming locations (Winter Sonata). Beautiful even in winter with snow-dusted trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Petite France (쁘띠프랑스) — a French-themed cultural village on the way back, also a famous K-drama filming site. Explore the colorful buildings and Le Petit Prince exhibits. Return to Seoul by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening — visit a Korean jjimjilbang (찜질방, Korean sauna/bathhouse) near the hotel for a cultural wellness experience. Gyeongbokgung area has several options. Soak, sweat, and relax like a local.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab kimbap and coffee from a convenience store or hotel. ~4,000–6,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Nami Island restaurant — try a Korean set meal on the island itself (the island has several dining options). ~15,000–18,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang snacks — a classic jjimjilbang experience includes eating sikhye (sweet rice drink) and hard-boiled eggs inside. Then grab a late dinner at a nearby 24-hour restaurant — try 해장국 (hangover soup) or instant ramyeon. ~8,000–12,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island entrance fee is ~16,000 KRW (includes ferry). Book Nami Island + Petite France combo tours from Myeongdong for convenience (~50,000–70,000 KRW including transport). Jjimjilbang entry typically costs 10,000–15,000 KRW. Bring a change of clothes and toiletries.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — a comprehensive and moving museum covering Korean history including the Korean War. Free admission for the main hall. Outdoor exhibits include military aircraft and tanks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) — a massive electronics bazaar great for K-tech gadgets, camera gear, and accessories. Then head to the Han River (한강) — visit Banpo Bridge area and walk along the riverside park. In winter, the frozen or near-frozen river views are stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower (남산타워) on Namsan Mountain — take the cable car up for panoramic night views of Seoul's city lights. See the famous love locks on the fence. The tower observation deck offers 360° views (~16,000 KRW).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — try a local 김치찌개 (kimchi jjigae) set at a neighborhood restaurant. ~8,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Yongsan area food court or nearby 부대찌개 (budae jjigae, Korean army stew) restaurant — a hearty, warming winter meal. ~12,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Namsan area or Myeongdong — Hadongkwan (하동관) for gomtang (beef bone soup), a Seoul institution since 1939. ~15,000 KRW. Or dine at a restaurant with Han River views near Banpo.

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial is closed on Mondays — perfect for Tuesday visit. N Seoul Tower cable car runs frequently but can have queues on weekends. The tower is also reachable by hiking up Namsan (about 40 min walk). Bring a padlock for the love lock fence — sold at the tower.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gangnam (강남) district — visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰), one of Asia's largest underground shopping complexes. Don't miss the stunning Starfield Library inside COEX — a floor-to-ceiling bookshelves installation that's become an iconic Seoul photo spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — a 1,000-year-old Buddhist temple dramatically set against Gangnam's modern skyline. Then explore Garosu-gil (가로수길) — a tree-lined boulevard famous for boutique fashion, cafés, and K-culture lifestyle shops.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Seoul's K-pop culture evening — visit SM Town COEX Artium (SM타운) for K-pop merchandise, holograms, and interactive K-pop experiences. Alternatively, visit a K-pop norebang (노래방, karaoke room) in Gangnam for an authentic group singing experience.

meals.breakfast: Gangnam-style café breakfast — visit a trendy specialty coffee shop in the area. Seoul's café culture is world-class. ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.lunch: COEX food hall — wide variety of Korean and international options. Try 쌀국수 (Vietnamese pho) or Korean 비빔밥 (bibimbap) set. ~12,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil restaurant — try Maple Tree House or a modern Korean cuisine restaurant. Or visit a 한정식 (hanjeongsik) restaurant for a traditional multi-course Korean meal — a mid-range splurge. ~25,000–35,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Bongeunsa Temple is free to enter and open daily. The juxtaposition of ancient temple against Gangnam skyscrapers is a must-see Seoul image. Norebang rooms typically cost 15,000–25,000 KRW/hour for a private room. COEX Starfield Library is free and open to the public.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) — a quieter, less-visited palace adjacent to Changdeokgung. Explore the beautiful grounds and greenhouse (온실). Then walk through the connected Jongmyo Shrine (종묘) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon Dynasty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a hip neighborhood of renovated hanok houses turned into trendy cafés, cocktail bars, and boutiques. One of Seoul's most photogenic and culturally rich neighborhoods. Perfect for afternoon wandering.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — head to Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) for the Christmas Eve atmosphere and potentially a midnight mass or carol service. The cathedral is beautifully decorated. Then enjoy the festive Myeongdong streets with Christmas markets.

meals.breakfast: Ikseon-dong area — visit a traditional hanok café for 식혜 (sikhye) and 떡 (tteok, rice cakes) or a modern brunch café. ~10,000–15,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Jongno area — try 낙지볶음 (spicy stir-fried octopus) or 곱창 (grilled intestines) at a traditional Jongno restaurant — adventurous local eating. ~12,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner — try a mid-range Korean fusion restaurant in Ikseon-dong or Insadong. Many restaurants offer special Christmas menus. ~25,000–35,000 KRW. Follow with hot 호떡 (hotteok) from a street stall.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is surprisingly festive — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday similar to Valentine's Day. Myeongdong Cathedral hosts special services. Book dinner reservations in advance as restaurants fill up quickly on Christmas Eve. Ikseon-dong is very Instagram-worthy.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning — visit Gyeongbokgung Palace one more time for a different experience, this time focusing on the National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) inside the palace grounds — free with palace admission. Excellent exhibits on traditional Korean life and customs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mapo/Hapjeong area — visit the Hongdae Book Street and Mangwon Market (망원시장), a beloved local traditional market less touristy than Gwangjang. Great for authentic local shopping and food grazing.
day_by_day.evening: Han River evening experience — visit Yeouido Hangang Park (여의도한강공원) for a winter Han River walk. Many Seoulites do this on holidays. Visit a nearby 치킨집 (fried chicken restaurant) for the quintessential Korean fried chicken and beer experience — a national comfort food tradition.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning treat — visit a bakery like Tartine or a hotel café for a Western-style Christmas breakfast. ~10,000–15,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market food stalls — graze on 순대 (sundae), 떡볶이 (tteokbokki), and 어묵 (fish cake). Very local, very affordable. ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Korean fried chicken restaurant near Yeouido or hotel — try Kyochon Chicken (교촌치킨) or BBQ Chicken for world-famous Korean fried chicken with beer (치맥). ~20,000–25,000 KRW for two

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions and restaurants remain open. Han River parks are free and open year-round. Layer up for the riverside — wind chill makes it feel much colder.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) — Seoul's spectacular mountain park right within the city limits. Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail (moderate difficulty, ~3-4 hours) for incredible views of Seoul from ancient fortress walls. Stunning in winter with possible snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from hiking by early afternoon. Visit the Eunpyeong Hanok Village (은평 한옥마을) near the park entrance — a newer hanok village with beautiful mountain backdrop. Grab a warming tea at a hanok café.
day_by_day.evening: Final major shopping evening — return to the Dongdaemun area for late-night shopping (many stores open until 5 AM). Great for last-minute K-fashion, accessories, and gifts. Visit the DDP night market.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike meal — 순두부찌개 (soft tofu stew) or 삼겹살 at a restaurant near the trailhead. ~9,000–12,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Mountain hiker's lunch — bring kimbap and snacks from a convenience store, or eat at a 산장 (mountain lodge) restaurant near the trail. ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Celebratory penultimate dinner — try a proper 갈비찜 (braised short ribs) or 전골 (hot pot) restaurant in the Jongno or Insadong area. ~20,000–28,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan hiking requires proper winter gear — ice cleats (아이젠) are strongly recommended in December and can be rented near the trailhead for ~3,000 KRW. Start early (8:00–9:00 AM) to complete the hike comfortably before dark (sunset ~5:30 PM). Trail map available at the park entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite neighborhood one last time. Seochon Village for a quiet morning walk, or Insadong for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit a traditional tea house (전통찻집) for a farewell cup of 유자차 (yujacha, citron tea) or 쌍화차 (ssanghwacha, herbal tea).
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and prepare for departure. If time allows, visit Gyeongbokgung's Heungnyemun Gate area for final photos of the palace exterior. Check out of the boutique hotel and head to the airport. Take AREX from Hongik University or Seoul Station to Incheon (~60-70 min). Arrive at least 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Browse duty-free shops for final Korean treats — Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts are excellent at the airport duty-free.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — 해장국 (haejangguk) or a neighborhood 백반집 (baekban, home-style Korean set meal) near the hotel. ~8,000–10,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Insadong area farewell lunch — try 쌈밥 (ssambap, rice wrapped in greens) or a traditional 비빔밥 at a well-regarded local restaurant. ~12,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Incheon — try the Korean food court options (신라면 or 비빔밥) or a sit-down restaurant in the departure terminal. ~15,000–20,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Airport is one of the world's best — arrive early to enjoy the transit cultural zone, Korean Cultural Street, and duty-free shopping. T-money card can be refunded at the airport (deposit returned). Keep some KRW for any final expenses before departure. Korean Air and Asiana duty-free offer excellent Korean snack sets and cosmetics for gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Private luxury transfer arranged via premium chauffeur service to boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Check-in, unpack, and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village, just minutes from the hotel. Wander the traditional alleyways of preserved Joseon-era hanok homes, absorb the atmosphere, and take in views of Gyeongbokgung Palace walls. Stop at a curated Korean craft gallery along Gahoe-ro.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mingles (Michelin-starred, modern Korean cuisine blending traditional jang fermentation with contemporary techniques). Afterward, a quiet nightcap walk along the illuminated walls of Gyeongbokgung Palace.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit; light snack at airport lounge if needed
meals.dinner: Mingles — tasting menu featuring seasonal Korean ingredients with wine pairing (Gangnam; worth the short taxi ride on arrival night)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive rested. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag management is key. Confirm hotel concierge for restaurant reservations upon landing. Gyeongbokgung area is walkable and calm in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace at opening (9:00 AM). Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate (10:00 AM & 2:00 PM). Explore the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds — exhibits on Joseon dynasty court life and Korean cultural heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Insadong for an immersive K-culture afternoon. Browse Ssamziegil courtyard's curated artisan shops, Korean ceramics, hanji paper crafts, and traditional tea accessories. Visit a premium Korean tea house for a private tea ceremony experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars, modern Korean fine dining). Post-dinner, explore the atmospheric lantern-lit streets around Insa-dong and Tapgol Park.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or nearby Tosokchon area café with traditional Korean morning spreads
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — temple food restaurant inside Jogyesa Buddhist complex (vegetarian, refined, deeply cultural)
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul — contemporary Korean tasting menu with Korean natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung opens at 9:00 AM (closed Tuesdays — confirmed Wednesday is open). Book Balwoo Gongyang in advance. Dress warmly — December temperatures average -2°C to 5°C in Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) via private guided tour. The winter garden — bare trees, frozen ponds, and snow-dusted pavilions — offers a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere unique to December.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a trendier, boutique-lined hanok neighborhood. Visit curated concept stores, Korean perfumeries, and independent galleries. Stop at a premium sikhye (traditional rice drink) or omija tea tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (3 Michelin stars, The Shilla Hotel) — the pinnacle of Korean haute cuisine. Reserve the private dining room for an exclusive experience with panoramic Seoul views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Gyeongbokgung-area café serving juk (Korean rice porridge) — try Juk Story or similar artisanal spot
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — curated premium bites: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare) at top stalls
meals.dinner: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel — 12-course Korean royal court cuisine tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tour at Changdeokgung requires advance booking — limited slots. La Yeon reservations should be made weeks in advance. Private car recommended for The Shilla.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) with a premium private guided tour. Visit Imjingak Park, the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station — the last train station before North Korea. Deeply moving cultural and historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul by 3:00–4:00 PM. Check into the hotel and refresh. Optional: visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (lesser-known, quieter, atmospheric in winter light).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — Korean royal court cuisine in an elegant, minimalist setting with a curated Korean liquor pairing featuring traditional makgeolli and soju varieties.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before DMZ departure (tours typically depart 7:30–8:00 AM)
meals.lunch: Lunch included or arranged near Imjingak — simple Korean army stew (budae jjigae) for cultural context, or packed premium bento from hotel
meals.dinner: Gaon — seasonal Korean tasting menu with Korean wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book DMZ private tour well in advance — passport required. Tour duration approximately 6–7 hours. Dress in warm layers; outdoor exposure at DMZ sites. Gaon is located in Gangnam — arrange private car.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, for a serene morning meditation experience. Participate in a private temple stay morning program — tea ceremony, meditation, and monk-led dharma talk. The temple's ancient zelkova trees are stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming, artsy neighborhood with independent bookshops, galleries, and traditional craft studios. Visit the studio of a noted Korean ceramic artist or calligrapher for a private hands-on workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Hansikgonggan (Michelin-starred, chef Cho Hee-sook's refined Korean home cooking elevated to art). Afterward, stroll through the Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) public grounds, now open to visitors.

meals.breakfast: Temple-style light breakfast of doenjang soup, rice, and seasonal namul (vegetable side dishes) as part of the morning program
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant steps from the hotel; a Seoul institution
meals.dinner: Hansikgonggan — seasonal Korean cuisine celebrating forgotten traditional recipes

day_by_day.notes: Seochon workshop requires advance booking through hotel concierge. Tosokchon may have queues even in winter — arrive slightly before noon. Blue House grounds are free to visit but check access hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums. Explore the Korean History Gallery, Buddhist Art Hall, and the stunning Cheongja (celadon) ceramic collection. Private curator-led tour recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon and Haebangchon area for a multicultural Seoul afternoon. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — world-class collection of traditional Korean art alongside contemporary international works in a Rem Koolhaas-designed building.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dosa (chef Corey Lee's Korean fine dining concept) or Onjium (Michelin-starred, deeply researched Korean culinary heritage). Explore Itaewon's premium cocktail bar scene afterward — try Charles H. at the Four Seasons or Zest Bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Anguk-dong café breakfast with artisan coffee and Korean pastries
meals.lunch: Namsangol Hanok Village area lunch — traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) at a refined restaurant near Namsan
meals.dinner: Onjium — rare royal court and regional Korean cuisine in a hanok-style setting

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — Sunday visit is ideal. Book Leeum Museum tickets in advance. Onjium requires reservations weeks ahead due to limited seating.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-culture immersion: visit a traditional hanji (Korean paper) studio in Jongno for a hands-on making session. Follow with a visit to the National Intangible Heritage Center to witness live demonstrations of Korea's UNESCO-recognized cultural traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) designed by Zaha Hadid — a futuristic landmark hosting design exhibitions and K-fashion showcases. Browse the adjacent Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. Visit premium Korean fashion concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mosu Seoul (Michelin-starred, chef Ahn Sung-jae's innovative Korean-influenced cuisine). Post-dinner, visit the Dongdaemun night market for a vibrant cultural contrast — street tteokbokki and hotteok as a casual late-night snack.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market premium sit-down experience — full Korean meal at one of the established family-run stalls known for japchae and jeon
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul — progressive Korean tasting menu with natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Hanji studio experience should be pre-booked. DDP exhibitions change seasonally — check current programming. December 21 is winter solstice — Dongdaemun at night has a festive atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's dramatic mountain backdrop. A guided winter hike to Bukhansanseong Fortress walls offers breathtaking snow-dusted panoramic views of the city. Moderate trail suitable for most fitness levels with proper winter gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Unhyeongung Palace — a lesser-known royal villa with intimate Joseon architecture. Then explore the nearby Nakwon Arcade for vintage Korean music instruments and rare K-pop memorabilia.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Joo Ok (Michelin-starred, Korean cuisine with deep respect for seasonal and local ingredients). Afterward, enjoy a traditional Korean music performance (gugak) at the National Gugak Center or a private nanta/pansori performance arranged by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early light hotel breakfast before hike
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal — premium sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a restaurant near Bukhansan entrance in Ui-dong
meals.dinner: Joo Ok — intimate Korean fine dining with seasonal omakase-style menu

day_by_day.notes: Bring proper winter hiking boots and layered clothing for Bukhansan. Trail may be icy — crampons available for rent at park entrance. Book gugak performance in advance through hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full K-beauty and wellness morning: private appointment at a luxury Korean spa (jjimjilbang experience elevated — try Dragon Hill Spa VIP section or Sulwhasoo Flagship Spa in Insadong). Traditional Korean body scrub (italy towel treatment), ginseng bath, and facial using K-beauty heritage brands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sulwhasoo Flagship Store and Museum in Insadong — a stunning space exploring the philosophy of Korean beauty rooted in hanbang (traditional medicine). Followed by a curated shopping experience at the Kukje Gallery or Arario Museum in Space.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve dinner at Ryunique (Michelin-starred, creative Korean-European fusion). Afterward, enjoy Seoul's festive Christmas illuminations — Cheonggyecheon Stream light festival and Gwanghwamun Square decorations are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light and healthy Korean set meal at a premium organic restaurant in Insadong or Anguk — try Plant or a refined hansik spot
meals.dinner: Ryunique — innovative tasting menu blending French technique with Korean soul

day_by_day.notes: Book spa appointments at least 3–4 days in advance. Sulwhasoo Flagship offers complimentary skin consultations. Cheonggyecheon light festival runs through winter — evening walk is magical in December.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace at dawn for a private, quiet experience before crowds arrive. Witness the palace in winter morning light — particularly magical with potential frost or snow. Private photography session with a professional Korean photographer arranged by hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Samcheong-dong — the chic gallery district connecting Gyeongbokgung to Bukchon. Visit independent art galleries, Korean design studios, and the Seoul Museum of History. Enjoy window shopping at premium Korean lifestyle brands.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve multi-course dinner at The Lounge at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul or a private chef's table experience. Afterward, join Seoul's festive Christmas Eve atmosphere around Myeongdong Cathedral — a beloved Seoul Christmas tradition.

meals.breakfast: Festive in-hotel Christmas breakfast spread or room service with Korean-Western fusion breakfast options
meals.lunch: Samcheong-dong café culture — premium lunch at a refined restaurant in the gallery district, seasonal Korean menu
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — Four Seasons Hotel Seoul festive tasting menu or private chef's table at a top restaurant (book 2+ weeks ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is festive and lively in Seoul — streets will be busy. Myeongdong Cathedral midnight mass is open to all. Hotel may offer special Christmas Eve amenities — confirm with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Christmas morning — sleep in, enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast. Optional: visit Jogyesa Temple for a peaceful Christmas morning contrast — Korean Buddhism and Christmas coexisting is a uniquely Seoul experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) — a picturesque river island famous for its tree-lined avenues, now dusted with winter frost and decorated for the season. A romantic and culturally rich escape made famous by the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.' Private car or premium train to Gapyeong.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul for Christmas dinner at Palais de Gaumont or a premium hotel restaurant. Alternatively, arrange a private Korean royal court dinner experience through the hotel with a private chef and traditional court music performance.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel Christmas breakfast — full spread with Korean and Western options
meals.lunch: Nami Island — picnic-style premium Korean lunch box prepared by hotel, or the island's restaurant with seasonal Korean dishes
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at a luxury hotel restaurant or private dining experience — festive Korean-Western fusion menu

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island is about 1.5 hours from Seoul — arrange private car for comfort. The island is beautiful in winter. Book Christmas dinner well in advance — restaurants fill up weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hongdae and Sinchon — Seoul's vibrant youth culture and K-pop epicenter. Visit the K-pop culture museum, browse independent music stores, and explore street art. Arrange a private K-pop studio session or dance class at a professional idol training studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam — visit the COEX Mall and its stunning Starfield Library. Explore the K-pop flagship stores (SM Town, HYBE Insight Museum). HYBE Insight offers an immersive behind-the-scenes look at K-pop production — book private guided tour.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Soil (chef Lim Jung-sik's new concept) or revisit a favorite Michelin-starred restaurant. Post-dinner: rooftop cocktails at Sky Bar at Lotte World Tower 123 (Seoul Sky observation deck + bar) for spectacular city views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Hongdae area brunch — premium brunch spot with Korean fusion menu
meals.lunch: Gangnam — premium Korean BBQ experience at Maple Tree House or Chadolbaegi & Ogyeopsal for premium wagyu-grade Korean beef
meals.dinner: Farewell fine dining — revisit top choice or try Soil/Evett for a memorable final evening

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight Museum requires advance booking — extremely popular. Seoul Sky observation deck at Lotte World Tower is open until late. Korean BBQ lunch is a must-do cultural experience — premium cuts only.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last stroll through Gyeongbokgung neighborhood and Bukchon Hanok Village for a peaceful farewell to the area. Visit a nearby antique shop or craft store for final souvenir purchases — premium Korean ceramics, hanji goods, or traditional lacquerware.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: visit Namdaemun Market for a final immersive Korean market experience and last-minute premium food purchases (dried seafood, premium teas, Korean sweets). Luxury private transfer to Incheon International Airport — allow 90 minutes minimum from central Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy the premium airport lounges (Korean Air First Class Lounge or Asiana Lounge are world-class). Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — casual but authentic final Korean meal: kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) or haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) at a beloved market stall
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Check out by hotel's standard time (typically 11:00 AM or 12:00 PM — confirm late checkout option). Arrange private airport transfer the night before. Pack Korean food items carefully — some fresh foods restricted. Keep receipts for VAT refund at airport (significant savings on luxury purchases).
